reason: Both correctly explain E:15 as water in the anti-flood tray, tell the homeowner to isolate power and water, and are honest that the leak source is unknown and needs an engineer. Conversation 1 asked the right rule-out question (detergent/foam), adapted usefully to the integrated-unit constraint with front-access drying, a single observed diagnostic run to note when/where water appears for the engineer, correct guidance on how integrated Bosch units actually slide out, and pointed to Bosch's fixed-price out-of-warranty repair. Its weakness is leaning towards repeated dry-and-retry rather than saying plainly 'book the engineer now'. Conversation 2 escalated more firmly but never ruled out foam or filter, twice gave instructions the homeowner could not follow, asked about spray arms the homeowner could not assess, and ended with repetitive, somewhat garbled text and no practical next steps beyond 'call someone'.
